recentItems.title: Putin's Rare 90-Minute Call With Finland & Norway On Ukraine War| Europe Furious, Zelenskyy Trapped?
recentItems.description:
The leaders of Finland and Norway reached out to Russian President Vladimir Putin by telephone in order to press him to bring the war in Ukraine to an end, a move that departs from a long-established habit among Western European leaders of avoiding direct contact with the Kremlin.

Finnish President Alexander Stubb and Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre made the call as an effort to exert influence over the diplomatic process, after Donald Trump changed his stance to side with Russia and relations between the United States and Ukraine fell to their lowest level in a year and a half.

Støre stated that he and Stubb had held a conversation with Putin that lasted roughly 90 minutes, after which they spoke with Volodymyr Zelenskyy, the President of Ukraine.

In a statement issued jointly, they connected this initiative to planned peace talks involving officials from Russia, Ukraine and the United States, which are set to take place in Abu Dhabi next month and would be the first such discussions since February.

While speaking with members of the Finnish press, Stubb stated that every Western ally had been consulted regarding the initiative, and he went on to note that Ukraine had asked for a new communications channel to be opened, adding that Europe could no longer stand by as a mere observer of the peace efforts.
